ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 5 — Preventive Visit — Jack London — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

text.paragraph: Mr. London is a 39-year-old writer with chronic kidney disease G3b A2 from hypertension and past naproxen use, severe alcohol use disorder in early recovery on naltrexone, alcohol-associated fatty liver and cigarette smoking, who comes for his preventive visit two weeks after his six-week review. He has not had a drink since the single evening four weeks ago after he sprained his ankle; the ankle is nearly back to normal. He writes every morning and has taken up a swim at the time he used to have his first drink. He has taken losartan 100 mg for two weeks without dizziness. His hepatitis B, hepatitis C and HIV tests drawn at the consultation were negative. He has not had an influenza or pneumococcal vaccine in years and has never had hepatitis A or B vaccines; his last tetanus booster was six years ago. He has not seen a dentist in several years. [S]

Follow-up: Ten-week review in two weeks with potassium, creatinine and PEth. Second hepatitis B dose at the twelve-week review. Next preventive visit in one year. Next scheduled visit 1915-10-13: ten-week review: abstinence, potassium and creatinine after the losartan increase, and the SGLT2 inhibitor. [S]

Voluntary advance care planning discussion of about 20 minutes, with his consent. He named a health care agent and completed a health care proxy form; the agent is recorded in the chart and is not named here. He said that what matters most to him is being able to think clearly and write, and to live on the ranch. He chose not to record specific treatment preferences now; the plan will be revisited if his kidney function falls further, and before any discussion of dialysis. [S]
